candidates.raw_excerpt:
A deep well has been completed at the northern edge of China's Taklimakan Desert, marking another breakthrough in the country's ultra-deep drilling capabilities.

At 6 pm on Friday, the Zhentan-1 well, located in Wensu County, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, reached a depth of 8,345 meters. It is the second ultra-deep well drilled using China's first domestically developed 12,000-meter drilling rig.

The well is designed to explore the oil and gas potential of large structural traps in the deep northwestern Tarim Basin, particularly those dating back to the Sinian Period, and to identify new areas for expanding oil and gas reserves.

The 12,000-meter rig features an 82-meter-high steel derrick capable of handling a maximum load of 665 tonnes and is designed to drill to depths of up to 12,000 meters. Its development means China no longer needs to rely on imported rigs for drilling wells deeper than 10,000 meters.

This marks the rig's second successful application. Equipped with a 6,000-horsepower drilling drawworks, the most powerful of its kind in China, and a 900-tonne lifting system, the rig can lift a load equivalent to two high-speed train sets. Its intelligent control system enables automated operations throughout the drilling process.

Google launched a prototype satellite into orbit on Thursday to evaluate how its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) operate in space.

The prototype satellite, carrying four Google TPUs, was launched aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission.

In low Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth, according to Google.

In the future, multiple satellite constellations could potentially be linked together, enabling them to handle larger AI workloads in orbit, the company said.

As per the letter he posted, the organizers were ordered to immediately stop hosting and promoting human-robot cage fights, or else face a misdemeanor charge. In its letter, the Athletic Commission didn’t appear to take issue with the human-robot bouts per se, but with the organizers’ failure to secure the required permits. That may be a distinction without a difference, however, as the Athletic Commission cited California business code which states that “no [full contact martial arts] event shall take place without the prior approval of the commission,” meaning the agency could simply withhold approval and veto a human-robot cage fight on a case-by-case basis — likely without ever having to explicitly declare such an event explicitly verboten. A power plant supporting China's first desert renewables mega base is now fully online.

Unit No.6 at the Zhongwei Power Plant in northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region successfully completed a 168-hour trial run on Friday.

The milestone brings all four 660-megawatt units into operation. The plant provides support during peak electricity demand for the Ningxia Tengger Desert renewables base and the ±800-kilovolt ultra-high-voltage direct current (UHVDC) line to Hunan.

The Tengger Desert base is the first project of its kind approved by both the National Development and Reform Commission and the National Energy Administration. It combines 13 million kilowatts of renewables – 4 million wind, 9 million solar – with 4.64 million kilowatts of coal-fired capacity to balance the grid.

The Zhongwei plant will provide stable back-up for the green power flowing out of the base. It smooths the gaps when wind and solar fall short by flexing its thermal output.

candidates.title: China develops new lithium battery material for faster charging
candidates.raw_excerpt:
A new cathode material developed by Chinese researchers could improve the fast-charging performance, durability and low-temperature operation of lithium-ion batteries.

A battery's cathode plays a key role in determining how much energy it can store, how quickly it can charge and discharge, and how long it can last. Researchers often add small amounts of specific elements to improve these properties.

A team from the Shenyang National Laboratory for Materials Science at the Institute of Metal Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, has developed a new strategy for selecting these trace elements based on their physical and chemical properties. The findings were published Thursday in the international journal Nature Synthesis.

The researchers focused on two challenges: enabling lithium ions to move more quickly through the cathode while keeping its structure stable during repeated charging and discharging.

They found that different elements can serve different functions. Some facilitate the movement of lithium ions through the material, while others strengthen its crystal structure.

The first effect is linked to an element's ionic charge density, which affects how easily lithium ions can move through the material. Elements with lower charge density create fewer obstacles to lithium-ion movement.

The second is related to the strength of metal-oxygen bonds. Elements that form stronger bonds with oxygen can reinforce the cathode's crystal structure, helping it withstand repeated charging and discharging.

Based on these principles, the team selected magnesium, calcium, titanium and zirconium to develop a cobalt-free, high-nickel cathode containing close to 1% of each element.

candidates.raw_excerpt:
Rising energy prices and the cost of living remain the biggest concerns in Southeast Asia regarding the transition to renewable energy and the phase-down of fossil fuels, a regional survey revealed on Thursday.

About 44.6% of respondents cited surging energy prices and living costs as their biggest concerns, according to the Southeast Asia Climate Outlook Survey Report 2026, launched by Singapore's ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute.

This was followed by concerns over energy shortages, cited by 26.1% of respondents, the report said.

Compared with the 2024 survey, the share of respondents concerned about rising energy prices and the cost of living fell from 52.4% to 44.6% in 2026.

At the same time, concern over energy shortages rose from 20.3% in 2024 to 26.1% in 2026. The report said these concerns may reflect disruptions caused by energy shocks and geopolitical events in recent years.

The 2026 survey gathered the views of 3,706 respondents across 11 ASEAN member states. It was the first edition to include respondents from Timor-Leste, ASEAN's newest member.

SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft carrying four astronauts for NASA's Crew-13 mission docked with the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday after a nearly eight-hour journey from launch to the orbiting laboratory.

The spacecraft lifted off at 11:10 a.m. aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. It autonomously docked with the ISS at 7:05 p.m.

The crew comprises NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov.

The mission, codenamed Crew-13, marks the 13th crew rotation mission to the ISS conducted by a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft under NASA's Commercial Crew Program.

The crew will spend several months aboard the space station conducting scientific research and technology demonstrations to support future human exploration of the moon and Mars, as well as studies with potential benefits for people on Earth, according to NASA.

candidates.raw_excerpt: A Falcon 9 rocket stands ready for launch from Vandenberg in this file photo. Image: SpaceX. An artificial intelligence prototype from Google, a methane-tracker, pharmaceutical manufacturing labs, and more are hitching a ride onboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket flying from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Thursday afternoon. The Transporter-18 mission is SpaceX second launch of the day, following the successful flight of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission from Florida. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4 East is scheduled for 11:32 a.m. PDT (2:32 p.m. EDT / 1832 UTC). The rocket will head off on a southerly trajectory upon leaving the pad. Spaceflight Now will have live coverage beginning about 30 minutes prior to liftoff. SpaceX will launch the mission using the Falcon 9 booster with the tail number B1082. This will be its 25th flight following the launches of NROL-145, USSF-62, and OneWeb Launch 20, and 21 batches of Starlink satellites. Nearly 7.5 minutes after liftoff, B1082 will target a landing back at Landing Zone 4. This will be the 36th landing at this site and 665th landing of a Falcon booster to date. The 130 payloads will be deployed into a polar orbit of the course of 11 minutes starting about 54 minutes into the flight.

CRC will lease 50 acres from the Greater London International Airport Authority for an engine test area and a 12,000-square-foot office and shop building used for engineering, assembly, and test preparation. Putting the shop next to the stands is meant to keep engine build-up, instrumentation, and test ops in one place rather than splitting that work across distant sites. The test area is planned for up to three vertical and horizontal stands, with the ability to static-fire engines producing more than 1 MN of thrust. Vertical stands are typically used for flight-like firings. Horizontal stands are often used earlier in a campaign for access, instrumentation, and engine development work. CRC said the site is a foundational step toward sovereign Canadian launch capability. The company expects the facility to be fully operational by 2028 and said it is working with the airport, regulators, and the local community as planning advances. candidates.title: Mate 90: Faster chips without the tools Huawei can't buy
candidates.raw_excerpt:
Huawei can't buy the machines that make the world's most advanced chips. So it redesigned the chip.

The Kirin 9050 Pro, launched inside the Mate 90 series on Thursday, is one of the first commercial processors built on LogicFolding – an architecture Huawei unveiled in May as the practical core of its "Tau Scaling Law." The company positions it as a successor to Moore's Law, as transistor shrinks approach physical and economic limits.

Instead of shrinking transistors, LogicFolding stacks two active circuit layers and links them with millions of vertical interconnects, shortening the distance signals must travel between logic blocks.

That answers a constraint Huawei consumer chief Richard Yu acknowledged days before the launch: "Advanced semiconductor capacity remains very limited in China," where chipmakers still depend on deep ultraviolet lithography rather than the extreme ultraviolet tools used at the leading edge.

Yu framed it in a single line: "Moore's Law pursues smaller transistors; Tau's Law pursues shorter, faster signal paths." CGTN previously described the approach as a move "from geometry to time," optimizing signal delay instead of transistor density.

The results are substantial. The Kirin 9050 Pro carries 5 million signal bonding points and delivers 125 TB/s of inter-die bandwidth. Huawei claims a 31% performance gain over the previous flagship generation, with critical-path latency cut by more than 30% – a figure that matters more for sustained workloads than peak benchmarks.

candidates.raw_excerpt: Slipping ratings, a revolving door of lead actors, and nothing quite hitting like that old school David Tennant run. It’s dog days for “Doctor Who” fans, whose lives aren’t likely to be made any better by the prospect of AI creeping into the show. While speaking at the Royal Television Society conference in London, BBC director Matt Brittin extolled the amazing efficiency of using AI to crank out footage — before raising the possibility of using it on one of the British broadcaster’s most beloved series. “Everyone’s got the ability in their hands — or six billion people have — to create content at the standard of a Hollywood studio,” Brittin said, as quoted by Variety . “Somebody sent me a 50-minute episode of ‘Doctor Who’ that was AI-generated the other day. It’s pretty good,” he continued. “I mean, it’s not going to replace humans, and we’ll come on to that. So everyone’s a creator.” Brittin, it’s worth noting, was president of Europe, Middle East, and Africa operations at Google — a major purveyor of AI tech — before joining the BBC . You have to wonder what Brittin’s idea of “pretty good” is. Attempts at using AI to crank out a movie or short film have invariably produced low grade slop . While the tech can sometimes create realistic images or scenes in isolation, cobbling together disparate, screensaver-worthy images together doesn’t constitute an episode of hit television. There’s a reason that filmmakers and other artists have turned their noses up at AI , along with the small matter of the tech threatening to drive them out of their jobs, and the fact that it was trained on their artwork and performances without permission. The ones that do use it get are often lampooned as hacks, has-beens or sellouts . candidates.raw_excerpt: SpaceX plans to launch a Transporter rideshare mission aboard a Falcon 9 from California, on the same day as the Crew-13 and NROL-97 Falcon Heavy missions out of Florida. This will be the first time in a while that the company is using all three Falcon-capable launch pads in the same general time period. Transporter 18 is scheduled to fly on Thursday, Oct. 1 at 11:18 AM PDT (18:18 UTC) from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The 58-minute launch window ends at 12:16 PM PDT (19:16 UTC), and if the schedule holds, this will be the 110th Falcon 9 mission of 2026. The mission’s 130 payloads feature a prototype AI satellite for Google, the NASA-funded SPRITE telescope, and Starfish’s first Otter servicing vehicle, among others. The rocket will take a southerly trajectory suitable for sun-synchronous orbiting payloads. Following stage separation, the first stage, B1082-25, will conduct a return-to-launch-site maneuver before touching down at Landing Zone 4 near its launch pad. The booster started its career with the Starlink 7-9 mission and launched on 20 additional Starlink flights, as well as the USSF-62, OneWeb #20, and NROL-145 missions. candidates.raw_excerpt: You can bundle your home and auto insurance with the click of a button, but covering your spacecraft has traditionally been a little trickier. CA-based Charter Space is working to increase access to insurance products for companies developing new missions in space, and yesterday it announced a $5M seed round to accelerate its market traction. Crystal Venture Partners led the round, which included participation from QED, Blank Ventures, Gaingels, Hustle Fund and others. The round brings Charter’s total financing to $8M since its founding in 2021.   In good hands: Before Charter came along, insuring spacecraft was a long and expensive undertaking, as underwriters—often without technical backgrounds—had to manually evaluate the combined risk of hundreds of subcomponents. The process kept space insurance largely out-of-reach to all but the most expensive missions—Charter CEO Yuk Chi Chan estimated earlier this year that ~97% of spacecraft in orbit are flying around uninsured. The Charter Interplanetary Risk Corporation (CIRC)—Charter’s own insurance brokerage for space companies—has been able to shorten this underwriting process by leaning on the technical expertise it gained through its space program management tool—called Ubik—which engineers rely on to build next-gen missions. CIRC married the data from Ubik with an AI-powered underwriting tool to shorten the time it takes to secure a policy, from months to approximately two weeks. And now, the company can hardly keep up with the wave of demand.
